title: Upload / Download Advanced
description: Upload, download, and response handling edge cases.

attacks.name: .htaccess upload
attacks.desc: Uploading .htaccess can change Apache behavior if uploads are served from a directory where overrides are honored.
attacks.prevention: Reject uploaded server configuration files, store uploads outside executable web directories, and disable overrides there.

attacks.name: web.config upload
attacks.desc: Uploading web.config can alter IIS behavior if the file is placed in an active configuration directory.
attacks.prevention: Reject web.config uploads and serve user files from storage that cannot change IIS configuration.

attacks.name: Filename path traversal
attacks.desc: An upload filename containing traversal syntax can escape the intended destination if path components are trusted.
attacks.prevention: Generate server-side storage names and canonicalize paths before enforcing an upload destination.

attacks.name: Filename null byte
attacks.desc: A null byte can cause legacy filename checks and file APIs to disagree about an extension.
attacks.prevention: Use modern file APIs and reject embedded nulls before extension or path validation.

attacks.name: Upload race condition
attacks.desc: A file changed between validation and storage can bypass upload checks that are not atomic.

attacks.name: Upload size limit bypass
attacks.desc: Chunking or inconsistent length checks can let uploads exceed an intended size limit.

attacks.name: Content-Type mismatch
attacks.notes: Extension vs MIME vs magic bytes
attacks.desc: A mismatch between extension, declared MIME type, and file signature can make an unsafe upload appear allowed.

attacks.name: SVG → SSRF
attacks.desc: An SVG renderer that fetches external references can be induced to request internal or remote URLs.

attacks.name: Range request abuse
attacks.desc: Range requests may expose unusual resource behavior or impose excessive work when limits are weak.

attacks.name: Partial content bypass
attacks.desc: If partial-content responses skip authorization, protected file ranges may be disclosed.

attacks.name: Download filename injection
attacks.desc: Untrusted filenames in Content-Disposition can inject or corrupt response headers if not encoded safely.
